messages:
Talia (Strategy): Quick Q from folks after the all-hands: how do we position pricing + packaging vs open-source self-hosted runtimes and the big cloud provider bundles? Need 1-2 lines for decks.

Jordan (CEO): Short: we sell predictable production outcomes, not just runtime. Line: 'Redwood turns raw models into predictable, cost-effective inference at scale across hosted, reserved, and private deployments 1 so teams hit latency and cost targets without building ops.'

Ben (Marketing): Can we make that two variants: a dev-focused and an exec-focused line?

Jordan (CEO): Dev line: 'Same API, one runtime, shipping production features (batching, KV cache, tooling) so engineers move faster.' Exec line: 'Predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and SLA-backed ops 1 better economics and lower risk than DIY or ad hoc cloud setups.'

Rach (Eng): Practical product question: when buyers ask "why not self-host?" what's our concise tech rebuttal?

Jordan (CEO): Tech rebuttal: 'Self-hosted runtimes require ops maturity (SRE, perf tuning, kernel/kernel-select), and ongoing maintenance. Redwood packages that work plus observability and fallbacks under an SLA.' Keep it factual.

Clara (Sales): Pricing hook for AMs: any suggested language for packaging vs cloud credits?

Jordan (CEO): Use a comparative hook: 'Instead of spending cycles on infra lift and tuning, customers trade predictable unit pricing + SLA for faster time-to-value. We quantify ROI via workload-specific benchmarks in our sales kit.'

Ben (Marketing): Action: I'll draft two slide blurbs and a one-pager ROI example. Rach: can you share an engineering note on maintenance burden differences we can reference?

Rach (Eng): Yep 1 I'll draft a short note (ops headcount, perf tuning hours, incident MTTR delta) and ping Marketing.

NotesBot: Recording + session notes uploaded: https://redwood.internal/recordings/2365412345 ; slides in /drive/all-hands/packaging-diff-note.pdf

Talia (Strategy): Great 1 thanks everyone. I'll put Jordan's lines in the strategy playbook and attach Ben's slide variants when ready.

Jordan (CEO): Thanks 1 keep follow-ups here.
